newsitem.title: UK: BOE warns on EMU complacency in financial sector.
newsitem.headline: BOE warns on EMU complacency in financial sector.

text.p: The Bank of England on Thursday warned the financial sector against complacency in its preparations for European monetary union (EMU).

"There may still be some complacency, perhaps because of expectations that the start date for EMU will be delayed," the Bank says in its latest review of progress on EMU preparations. "Such a view would be a high-risk strategy."
The Bank concludes that for planning purposes, the only prudent assumption is that EMU will begin on time.
The central bank also warns banks and other financial institutions that the long lead-times involved in changing even moderately complex IT systems must be taken into account.
"The planning stage may well need to be completed and development to have begun within the next few months," the BOE said.
Banks must allow a sufficient period for trialling ahead of the beginning of 1999, when the first wave of countries is expected to launch a single currency.

The Bank said that the development of a UK wholesale payments system to embrace the euro from the beginning of 1999 is proceeding on schedule. This will go ahead regardless of whether the UK is in the first wave of countries or not.
